What to Eat for Healthier Skin and Slower Aging

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 11 min read (2108 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Elle

⏱️ ~11 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Every item on this page was chosen by an ELLE editor.
  • On the quest to age smarter and slower, there’s a lot that your skin care can do.
  • To understand the connection between diet and skin health, Caitlin Hosmer, MS, RD, LDN, a registered dietitian and co-founder of MenoPantry, indicates it’s key to define the notion of slowing down aging.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Every item on this page was chosen by an ELLE editor. We may earn commission on some of the items you choose to buy.

On the quest to age smarter and slower, there’s a lot that your skin care can do. But perhaps one of the greatest contributions lies in the foods you consistently eat. Of course, diet and exercise are the pillars of good health, proper body function, and longevity, but a recent study done by scientists at the German Center for Neurodegenerative Diseases (DZNE) also reveals that 10 specific diets are linked to slower aging. Experts unpack the findings for ELLE and break down which foods you should incorporate or ditch from your diet to help improve skin health.

To understand the connection between diet and skin health, Caitlin Hosmer, MS, RD, LDN, a registered dietitian and co-founder of MenoPantry, indicates it’s key to define the notion of slowing down aging. She points out that this particular DZNE study didn’t look at wrinkles or how old people feel. “It looked at biological aging, measured with epigenetic clocks. These read chemical marks on our DNA (methylation) that shift as our cells age. In about 7,500 adults, the researchers found that following any of 10 healthy eating patterns more closely was associated with slower biological aging,” Hosmer explains. The 10 eating patterns or diets included in the study results are Mediterranean, Nordic, DASH, MIND, and plant-based. Hosmer says that while the effect was modest, this kind of study highlights an association, not causation—proof that diet is the reason for the positive outcome—so it is still a meaningful signal.

Additionally, Mark Gilbert, nutritionist from The 1:1 Diet by Cambridge Weight Initiative, tells ELLE that no single food has been satisfactorily studied and shown to be likely, on its own, to slow aging. “Of all the predictors of a long, healthy life, two of the best, which can be improved with diet, are muscle mass and strength, but this leads to a controversial conclusion,” indicates Gilbert. “The best nutritional intervention to increase muscle and strength is eating a high-protein diet. However, many scientists argue that high-protein diets have the opposite effect on longevity. So, if we can’t even agree on that, you can see that science has a long way to go to try and figure this out.”.

One stat Hosmer found particularly striking was that over 70 percent of the biological pathways affected were the same across all ten diets. “I interpret that to mean that no single superfood is doing the work, and it affirms that [a combination of] food, diet, and nutrition impacts us on the cellular level. The foods these patterns share are what matter,” indicates Hosmer, who, along with Gilbert, breaks down the standouts:.

Industry observers note that alongside individual foods, Hosmer claims certain diet components have the greatest impact on aging. For starters, protein is a must. “As we age, our muscles respond less efficiently to the protein we eat. This is called anabolic resistance, and in women, the drop in estrogen makes it worse,” she explains. Building and retaining muscle isn’t only about strength; Hosmer says it’s our largest site for handling blood sugar and a strong predictor of independence later in life. “Many women eat less protein just when they need more.”.

Gilbert adds that while protein is an important part of a balanced, longevity diet, there are some considerations to keep in mind before adding it to your meal. “I believe that because muscle and strength are so strongly associated with longevity and that protein, particularly later in life, supports them,” he says. The caveat, however, is that there is a potential mechanism (which has to do with the amino acid methionine) whereby too much protein could have negative effects. “Many scientists argue that, because in insects and some other animals, less protein along with calorie restriction increases lifespan, humans would similarly benefit. Also, some cite the so-called ‘Blue Zones’, alleged to show that plant-based, low-protein diets are superior. In my opinion, all of these have been shown to be invalid,” says Gilbert.

It has been revealed that fiber is another essential nutrient that you’ll reap from plant foods and mushrooms. Meat, fish, dairy, and eggs contain no fiber, and because our enzymes can’t break them down, Hosmer notes that fiber travels intact to the large intestine to assist. Once there, fermentable fibers become food for the gut microbiome; other fibers mainly add bulk and keep things moving. “As gut bacteria ferment fiber, they make short-chain fatty acids, which nourish the cells lining the gut, help keep that barrier strong, and keep inflammation in check. Fiber also steadies blood sugar and helps the body excrete estrogen the liver has already processed, supporting healthy hormone balance. Yet more than 90 percent of American women don’t reach the recommended 21 to 25 grams a day,” Hosmer explains.

According to recent reports, plant diversity matters, too, and not just quantity. Hosmer points to research from the American Gut Project that found people who ate 30 or more different kinds of plant foods a week had more diverse gut microbiomes than those who ate 10 or fewer. “That’s because each plant brings its own mix of fibers and polyphenols, and some bacteria have preferences, so a varied diet feeds a broader community of microbes. A broader community does more jobs. It makes short-chain fatty acids that protect the gut lining, helps regulate immunity and inflammation, turns plant compounds into forms the body can use, and even helps process estrogen.” The variety of plants Hosmer adds seems to matter more than any single “perfect” plant.

Sources indicate that you’ve likely heard of healthy fats, meaning omega-3s from fish and the polyphenol-rich fat in olive oil. Adding these to your diet can support cell membranes and help settle inflammation.

In a recent development, also on the list for Gilbert is vitamin D, which he says studies have shown to be inversely related to the risk of mortality. “This does not prove that low vitamin D is the cause, but it is compelling evidence. Although some results are controversial, low [vitamin D] levels have been linked to all-cause, cardiovascular, cancer, and infection-related mortality,” he adds. Vitamin D is intimately involved in immunity, too. It protects T-cell immune response.

In a recent development, although Gilbert notes, “The only thing all good nutritionists agree on is that there is no one ‘best’ diet or ‘best’ food,” he warns that for most people, minimizing the intake of sugar and refined, starchy grains and increasing protein intake is, in my opinion and experience, the best approach, but, again, different people can thrive on different diets. “As in the examples I gave, many of these foods contain phytochemicals—plant chemicals like polyphenols, flavanols, cyanidins, and others – which affect disease risk or support systems in the body that are likely to serve you well in old age.”.

Industry observers note that hosmer notes several other red flags as contributing to unhealthy skin: Diets dominated by refined carbohydrates and added sugars, heavily processed meat, and regular alcohol. “Each of these drives the chronic, low-grade inflammation researchers call “inflammaging,” and blood-sugar instability.”.

Having seen so many gaps in these important nutrients in her practice, and understanding how women’s bodies change in midlife, led Hosmer and her team to build Menomix at MenoPantry. “One serving adds meaningful protein along with ground flaxseed and psyllium fiber, plus a range of plant ingredients. It’s made to help close the protein, fiber, and plant-variety gaps that so many women are carrying,” she adds.

To dive deeper into some of those gaps or bad habits that can send skin aging off the rails, Hosmer offers some eating patterns that push biology in the wrong direction:.

The information can be overwhelming, but instead of purging everything in your fridge, Hosmer suggests first focusing on adding good foods instead of restricting less healthful options. “In my experience, that’s more sustainable, both because it feels less like deprivation and because the “good” foods can displace the ones that speed aging up instead of slowing it down. You don’t need to pick the “right” diet and follow it perfectly.”.

It has been revealed that she highlights that the DZNE study found few people scored well on all ten diets at once, yet better adherence to any of them helped. What matters is the common ground. Mediterranean, Nordic, DASH, MIND, and plant-based diets vary on the plate, but they have a common core: more fruits, vegetables, and whole grains, and less red and processed meat, and added sugar. “That shared core is where I’d start,” indicates Hosmer, offering this meal planning guide:.

Increase your familiarity with, and use of, plant-based proteins. Plant-based proteins offer an excellent package of beneficial nutrients, including fiber (not found in animal products). If you aren’t already familiar, learn how to include whole soy foods (tofu, tempeh, edamame) in your diet; add beans and peas and lentils to dishes here and there. Nuts and seeds and nut and seed butters count here also.

In a recent development, build meals around vegetables and fruit. Fill half your plate with them, and choose deep colors like leafy greens, berries, beets, and cabbage-family vegetables. Those colors come from polyphenols, plant compounds that act as antioxidants and feed beneficial gut bacteria.

Make your grains whole and varied. Oats, rye, barley, brown rice, and whole-wheat bread are staples of the Nordic and DASH patterns, the two most consistently linked to slower aging in this study. Try a grain you haven’t eaten before—quinoa? Farro? Millet or teff? They are all cooked the same way—in boiling water, just with different grain-to-water ratios. Note: raise fiber gradually, with plenty of water, so your gut has time to adjust.

According to recent reports, count your plants, not your calories. Aim toward 30 different kinds of plant foods a week. Veggies, fruits, nuts, seeds, whole grains, beans, peas, herbs, and spices all count. A homemade trail mix, an interesting salad, or a smoothie with a handful of fruit and veggies can add three or four at once.

Sources indicate that choose your fats deliberately. Most of these patterns favor unsaturated fats over saturated ones. Use extra-virgin olive oil as your everyday fat, and eat oily fish two or three times a week.

It has been revealed that keep red and processed meat occasional, and keep added sugar low. Every one of these diets limits them.

It has been revealed that quality matters. Note that “plant-based” isn’t automatically healthy. A version of the plant-based diet built on refined grains, sweets, and sugary drinks tended to be associated with faster aging, as did a pro-inflammatory eating pattern overall. Food quality matters, not just food category.

It has been revealed that diet is the foundation the other efforts rest on. Collagen supplements and skin care can help, but they can’t make up for a body that lacks what it needs to build and protect tissue. According to Gilbert, collagen supplements contain very high levels of the amino acid glycine, which he says can balance the potential harms of proteins that are high in methionine.

Hosmer further explains that collagen peptides break down during digestion into amino acids and small peptides. Your body then decides where to use them. “To actually build collagen, it needs enough total protein, plus vitamin C. Vitamin C is a required helper for the enzymes that stabilize the collagen structure. It also needs minerals like zinc and copper. So a collagen supplement taken on top of a protein-poor, micronutrient-poor diet is not going to be optimized,” Hosmer states. “Collagen is also an incomplete protein: it’s low in leucine and lacks tryptophan entirely. It can add to your protein intake, but it isn’t a substitute for complete proteins when it comes to muscle.”.

On the surface, what we eat affects the skin from the inside. Hosmer notes that polyphenol-rich foods and healthy fats support the skin’s own defenses against oxidative stress, and high blood sugar leads to glycation, which stiffens collagen fibers. The gut matters here, too. “Researchers call the connection the gut–skin axis. When the gut lining is healthy, and the microbiome is well fed, inflammation throughout the body tends to stay lower, and the skin reflects that. External products can only do so much if we aren’t supporting our skin from the inside,” Hosmer says.

Recent findings suggest that diet plays a major role in overall skin health and slower aging, but Hosmer argues that it’s not the full picture. To optimize more youthful-looking skin, consider other factors that may be equally as important as diet.

The 5 Types of Coats Every Guy Should Own

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 9 min read (1800 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Esquire

⏱️ ~9 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Years ago, I was talking to a very menswear-y buddy at a very menswear-y event, and he proposed a theory of outerwear that’s stuck with me: Your coat is your car.
  • It has been revealed that no, your coat cannot help you travel at 75 miles per hour down an interstate.
  • It has been revealed that but if you live in a place where you spend more time walking or taking public transit than you do behind the wheel, your coat does indeed become quite car-like.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Years ago, I was talking to a very menswear-y buddy at a very menswear-y event, and he proposed a theory of outerwear that’s stuck with me: Your coat is your car. Sounds pretty … menswear-y, right? But bear with me here, because I think it actually makes perfect sense, so long as you’re willing to make a couple (major) concessions.

It has been revealed that no, your coat cannot help you travel at 75 miles per hour down an interstate. You cannot fill it up with gasoline or top it up at a charging station. It contains, ideally, zero percent steel.

It has been revealed that but if you live in a place where you spend more time walking or taking public transit than you do behind the wheel, your coat does indeed become quite car-like. You ensconce yourself in it when you move about the world. It’s the first thing people see when you arrive and the last thing they see when you depart. It shields you from the elements while simultaneously signaling to friends and strangers alike your combined senses of utility and aesthetics. So, yeah, if you squint and look at the situation sideways, your coat is your car. Even if you live somewhere that demands personal automotive transportation, your coat is your second car—unless you’re one of those kooky types who just dart from the interior of a sedan to the interior of a restaurant in nothing but a sweater—for all the reasons stated above.

The point is: Your coat is the most visible and functional part of your winter wardrobe, and you should approach the buying and wearing of said coat with all due respect for its position. Which is exactly why I created this guide. We’ll run through the key styles that every guy should know, where to get a great example (or three!) of each, and how to wear them with style all season long. You won’t find truckers or bombers here—those are jackets—but you will find parkas, topcoats, trenches, and more. All of them will serve you well until the spring thaw, so let’s get into it.

If you’ve been keeping up with Esquire style guides, you’ll know that we’ve covered a lot of ground over the past few years, breaking down everything from the shoe styles you should have in your rotation to the winter essentials you shouldn’t go without. One story that really resonated with readers was about sweaters. In it, we talked about the fact that you can score very good knitwear from a huge range of lifestyle brands these days. We also mentioned the prudence of keeping a few category specialists on your radar. The same advice holds true for coats.

On the lifestyle side, the brands will look familiar to longtime readers. You’ve got Todd Synder and Buck Mason. J. Press and J. Crew. Ralph Lauren and Drake’s and Alpha Industries and Madewell and Billy Reid and Filson ... the list goes on. You’ve also got fashion behemoths like Burberry, which famously started out with the trench coat. And then you’ve got brands that may not just do outerwear but are truly steeped in it. That could be a heritage player like Mackintosh or Schott or Gloverall, a parka expert like Canada Goose, or an upstart label like Wythe, which makes a wonderful range of products but has a cult following for its exceptional overcoats.

Recent findings suggest that as we’ve warned before: This list is not exhaustive. But it’s a good place to start. Now, on to the coats themselves.

In a recent development, this is the dressiest of the bunch, though it wasn’t always. If you’re a real traditionalist, you might have a velvet-collared Chesterfield in your closet to wear with your fanciest togs. Most of us, though, don’t really need something that formal. The topcoat is similar to and derives from the Chesterfield, but it’s less stuffy.

Still, it looks plenty dressed up to modern eyes. It’ll have lapels, which can be notch or peak (for a little extra personality), and can be single- or double-breasted. If you suit up with any regularity, that means it’s likely the most essential for your wardrobe. Look for one made of wool or a wool blend; this is not the time to overspend on synthetics.

Industry observers note that colors are usually pretty conservative—think camel, navy, gray, and black. That might seem limiting, but remember that this thing should be able to play nicely with your whole wardrobe, so opting for a more subdued hue is usually the right move. As for length: Some folks will swear something that hits above the knee looks more modern. We just think it looks off. Go for at or below the knee.

(Oh, and if you’re wondering if a classic polo coat really counts as a topcoat as opposed to an overcoat, well, you might be right to question us. Technically. But considering its cultural associations—rich Upcoming Englanders, Wall Street power brokers—we’re giving it a home here.).

Todd Snyder Italian Gramercy Topcoat.

Polo Ralph Lauren Camel-Hair Polo Coat.

Industry observers note that eschewed by many as a bit too fusty and old-fashioned as recently as a decade ago, the raglan overcoat has come roaring back into the spotlight in recent years. We enthusiastically endorse its return.

Sources indicate that the style is defined by its raglan shoulder construction, in which a diagonal seam runs from around the collarbone to the underarm, allowing for an uninterrupted panel over the top of the shoulder. Don’t worry too much about the technical details, though. The main thing to remember is that this shape is more relaxed and tends to layer over other garments (a chunky sweater, a sport coat) more easily and comfortably than a traditional “set in” shoulder seam.

Sources indicate that the raglan overcoat also tends to be cut wide and long, so you can bundle up underneath it and never worry about chilly knees. It leans more casual than a topcoat, for sure, but you can still wear it with a suit. And it lends polish to something as simple as jeans and a sweatshirt. One of our favorite subgenres of raglan overcoat is the balmacaan, which features a Prussian collar (which looks like a shirt collar instead of a lapel), a “fly front” with a placket that covers the buttons, and buttoned fasteners at the wrists so you can cinch up to keep out the cold.

Buck Mason Donegal Tweed Balmacaan.

Wythe Raglan Overcoat in Diamond Ombre Tweed.

Salt and Pepper Wool Raglan Coat.

According to recent reports, if you’re into the warm and wooly vibes of the two styles above but simply can’t stand a long coat, the peacoat is for you. Double-breasted and hip length, it’s a shorter—but no less capable—take on the woolen overcoat that dates back about three centuries.

Originally created for sailors of European (and, eventually, American) navies, the peacoat is tough enough to defend from open-ocean winds and sea spray, which means it’s definitely up to the task of keeping you toasty on your way to work. There are a lot of versions out there these days that are done up in frankly wimpy wool blends that might feel nice at first but don’t do the job.

Sources indicate that go for a heavyweight wool like melton, but make sure there’s enough room to layer up underneath it—and keep an eye on the lapels. They should be big. Big enough that you can pop that collar and shield yourself from an incoming gust without feeling even a tickle of wind touch your neck. Plus, it looks cool.

It has been revealed that J. Crew Dock Peacoat in Wool Blend with PrimaLoft.

Thanks to a quirky little phenomenon we like to call “global climate change,” there’s a very good chance that some of the winter days ahead will feel a lot more like fall or spring. On those days—especially if it’s raining—you should reach for a trench coat or a mac. The two styles aren’t synonymous, but they’re related in both vibe and history, so we’re coupling them here.

Industry observers note that maximalists will prefer the trench, with its storm flap and epaulettes and double-breasted closure. Minimalists will reach for the mac, with its clean lines and streamlined shape. It’s really a matter of preference, because both fulfill the same roles in your outerwear lineup.

Recent findings suggest that they’ll keep you warmish, especially when combined with additional layers. They’ll help block the wind when it kicks up. And although we can’t guarantee you’ll walk away dry if you stand around for an hour during a deluge, they’ll fend off a shower—or a sprint through a thunderstorm—quite capably.

Mackintosh Dunkeld Raintec Coat.

Burberry Long Kensington Heritage Trench Coat.

If it’s really fucking frigid, you need a parka. Make sure it’s properly insulated, whether with a synthetic fill or down. And unless you like freezing your literal ass off, get one that’s hip length or longer. You could get something technical and bright that looks like it just stepped off the ski slopes, but we’re more inclined toward rugged-looking styles that take their cues from the military and outdoor exploration.

It has been revealed that the N-3B, or “snorkel parka,” is a burly beast that looks absolutely fantastic with a casual outfit and, if you ask us, can be fun with a suit too. (Though if you’re worried about raising eyebrows or breaking a dress code, maybe opt for a topcoat instead.) Something like Canada Goose’s Langdon parka is a little more pared back in looks but overdelivers on warmth, meaning you’ll be cozy in even the worst weather. The trick is finding one that balances form and function so that it looks as though you intended to wear it on the way to the bar—not like you wandered off some snowcapped mountain and forgot to change.

Moose Knuckles Stirling Down Parka 2.0.

Canada Goose Langford Parka Black Disc.

Industry observers note that like the peacoat, the duffle coat is a part of maritime history. It was adopted by the British Royal Navy in the late 19th century and widely issued to British troops during World War II. Thanks to the sheer number produced and postwar surplus, it swiftly became a civilian staple and eventually hopped across the pond to become a fixture of the American preppy uniform. Made of thick wool and equipped with a big hood, it’s very warm. And thanks to the large toggle closures, you don’t even need to take your gloves off to fasten it. Is it a little odd? Perhaps. But that’s what makes it so charming.

Industry observers note that J. Press Made-in-England Classic Morris Duffle Coat.

Gloverall Men’s Original Monty Duffle Coat.

  • According to recent reports, brands like Saatva, Birch, and Beautyrest are already offering up to $1,000 off on hotel-worthy innerspring mattresses, cooling hybrids, and organic options.
  • Sources indicate that below, you'll find AD-tested mattresses, complete with reviewer insights, notable features, and details about the current promotions.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, black Friday isn't until November 27, but that hasn't stopped mattress brands from getting a head start on the holiday savings. If your current bed has seen better days or you're waking up with more aches than you went to bed with, there's no need to wait until a designated shopping day to save big on an upgrade. We've spotted the 12 best Black Friday mattress deals to explore ahead of all of your Thanksgiving festivities.

According to recent reports, brands like Saatva, Birch, and Beautyrest are already offering up to $1,000 off on hotel-worthy innerspring mattresses, cooling hybrids, and organic options. Whether you're a side sleeper in need of a little extra cushioning for your hips and shoulders or someone who prefers a firmer, more supportive surface, there's something worth considering before the holiday rush kicks into high gear.

Sources indicate that below, you'll find AD-tested mattresses, complete with reviewer insights, notable features, and details about the current promotions. Get ready to find your next bed without losing sleep over the price tag.

In a recent development, saatva is giving shoppers who have “luxury mattress” on their Black Friday wish list a head start on savings. The brand is taking over $600 off its popular Classic queen. Designed to deliver hotel-worthy comfort at home, the innerspring mattress features a dual-coil construction; a plush, three-inch Euro pillow top; and targeted lumbar support that helps promote spinal alignment. It also comes in three firmness options—plush soft, luxury firm, and firm—making it a versatile choice for different sleep positions. Reviewer Erin Kaplan, a combination side-and-stomach sleeper, praises the mattress's supportive feel, durability, and temperature regulation. “Overall, I get a better night’s sleep on a more consistent basis since I switched mattresses,” she says. Complimentary white-glove delivery, a 365-night sleep trial, and a lifetime warranty round out the perks of this high-end buy.

Another name brand with an impressive 180 years of history, Stearns & Foster has a reputation for hotel-quality bedding you’ll find in luxury hotel chains like the Ritz-Carlton. They’ve already kicked off their Black Friday sale, which promises up to $1,000 off select adjustable mattress sets and a $300 Visa gift card with all mattress purchases. Senior visuals editor Melissa Maria raves about her Stearns & Foster Lux Estate Mattress, noting its seamless white glove delivery service was a game-changer. The level of firmness required an adjustment period for her, but the Tempur-Indulge memory foam layer and added pillow top gave it a more plush feel. “I’m a very light and finicky sleeper and it always takes me time to adjust to any sort of change, but my husband remarked at how well he slept and how much better his back felt after the first couple of nights sleeping on this mattress,” she indicates.

In a recent development, beautyrest’s long-lasting mattresses are powered with advanced pocketed coil technology, helping couples with motion isolation and providing zoned support. The brand’s Black Friday sale is underway, and you can now save up to $1,000 on select mattress and adjustable base sets. Audience development manager Emma Tubbs recommends the Beautyrest Black Series One Mattress, which she claims has the “perfect firmness.” “As someone who continuously changes positions throughout the night, the quilted innerspring construction nicely accommodated my tossing and turning,” she writes in her review. “I often fall asleep on my stomach and move to my side and even my back as I fall deeper into REM—I feel supported by this mattress in each position.” Plus, the motion isolation has worked well for her, as she continues sleeping through her husband’s 5:30 a.m. wakeups.

It has been revealed that over the past century, Serta’s become known for making comfortable, solidly priced mattresses. As it stands, the brand is offering the lowest price we’ve seen in months on the Serta Five-Star Mattress. Shopping writer Julia Harrison had this mattress-in-a-box delivered downstairs, and managed to haul it up with the help of her roommate. She refers to it as relatively lightweight (thanks to the gel-infused foam versus a heavier gel bead layer), exactly medium-firm, and made without any frills. “Nothing about it feels too hard or too soft, which I know primarily because I never think about the density or firmness of this mattress (a good sign!) and because I’ve had no back or neck problems since sleeping on it,” she notes.

It has been revealed that selecting a firmer mattress doesn't mean you’re opting for less comfort. That’s especially true with the original PurpleFlex bed-in-a-box, currently $100 off ahead of Black Friday. Unlike traditional memory foam beds, the PurpleFlex features a two-inch GelFlex Grid designed to relieve pressure while maintaining a supportive, responsive feel. Beneath that layer, a durable foam base provides stability, making the eight-inch mattress especially appealing to back and stomach sleepers who prefer sleeping on top of their bed rather than sinking into it. AD tester Chapin Rockwell particularly likes the firm construction, reporting “less back pain and stiffness” after switching to the PurpleFlex.

The WinkBed is a luxury hybrid mattress that caters to your preferred sleeping style, and it’s right now 30% off as part of the brand’s Veterans Day sale. What makes the WinkBeds particularly versatile is its four firmness options: Softer, Luxury Firm, Firmer, and Plus (the last level, Plus, is designed for sleepers who need additional support). Beneath its plush yet supportive Euro pillow top, pressure-relieving gel foam and individually wrapped coils work together to provide cushioning, targeted support, and motion isolation. A moisture-wicking Tencel cover also helps promote a cooler sleeping environment. But don’t just take WinkBeds’ word for it. Contributor Mark Burka notes that the mattress "provides strong edge support and wicks away heat," two features that help distinguish it from other hybrids. Moreover, it also comes with free shipping, a 365-night sleep trial, and a lifetime warranty, offering plenty of time to determine whether it's the right fit for you.

It has been revealed that side sleepers searching for a more supportive night's rest should put shopping Nolah's early Black Friday sale at the top of their shopping list. Shopping editor Audrey Lee, who tested an earlier iteration of the Evolution, praises its high level of comfort and cooling abilities. “I found this design’s contouring quality top-tier for pressure relief, but I still had ample support thanks to the coils,” she says. The brand is right now taking 35% off its mattresses, bringing the queen-size Evolution from $2,277 down to $1,480. Designed to cushion sensitive pressure points without sacrificing support, the luxury hybrid combines responsive AirFoam Luxe, individually wrapped coils, and targeted lumbar support to help keep the spine aligned. Shoppers can choose among Plush, Luxury Firm, and Firm options, all of which can accommodate an optional GlacioTex cooling pillow-top upgrade for additional cushioning and temperature regulation. A 365-night sleep trial, free shipping, and a limited lifetime warranty make the early holiday deal even sweeter.

To make your bedroom a little more environmentally conscious, consider starting with the Birch Natural Mattress, a medium-firm hybrid model that’s free of polyurethane foam, fiberglass, formaldehyde, and pesticides. Instead, it’s made from natural and organic materials, including breathable organic cotton, natural wool, and organic latex that’s certified by the Global Organic Latex Standard (GOLS), breathable organic cotton, and natural wool. Individually wrapped steel coils provide responsive support, while the latex offers gentle contouring (as opposed to the sinking feeling you might get from memory foam). Contributor Zoë Sessums was particularly impressed by the mattress's balance of softness and firmness, calling its feel "Goldilocks perfection." #66242. “It Was Never About Fashion”: Emily in Paris’s Costume Designer Reveals the Method to Her Madness

📅 19 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 6m • 📚 Deep Dive (1136 w)
📖 Baca

“It Was Never About Fashion”: Emily in Paris’s Costume Designer Reveals the Method to Her Madness

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1136 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Harpersbazaar

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Emily in Paris premiered when audiences needed it most.
  • The love for Emily in Paris was anything but unanimous.
  • For six seasons, Fitoussi curated a wardrobe fit for Emily, a bright-eyed young woman unafraid to try something upcoming, to break the rules.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Emily in Paris premiered when audiences needed it most. The Netflix original, created by Sex and the City producer Darren Star, offered an escapist fantasy: a young girl trying to find love and success in Paris in October 2020. The show functioned as a reprieve from the pandemic, a dreamy alternative in which we could vicariously live through Emily (Lily Collins) as she gallivanted around the City of Light. It was and still is delectably digestible television.

The love for Emily in Paris was anything but unanimous. Critics wasted no time tearing the show apart, with some targeting its depictions of French culture or claiming the script lacked the bite of Star’s previous television shows. The criticism extended to Emily’s idiosyncratic wardrobe, with some writing that the clothing leaned hard on American stereotypes of French fashion or looked cartoonish, with clashing patterns and bright colors. Costume designer Marylin Fitoussi took these criticisms head-on and doubled down. Emily’s outfits weren’t meant to be couture or designer; they were meant to dress a girl finding her sense of self, expressing her desire to explore the unknown.

For six seasons, Fitoussi curated a wardrobe fit for Emily, a bright-eyed young woman unafraid to try something upcoming, to break the rules. This mirrors Fitoussi’s personal philosophy on clothing: that fashion is meant to break rules, to push boundaries, to provide a space of unrelenting experimentation. Ahead of the sixth season, SCAD FASH Museum of Fashion + Film compiles six seasons’ worth of outfits in “Emily in Paris: Fashion Without Rules,” on view through March 14, 2027. The exhibition lives up to its name; for the designer, clothing is a mode of expression that lets anyone feel free, wherever they are. It offers a character study, tracing Emily’s evolution from a doe-eyed expat to a well-versed Parisian resident. (And worry not, there are also looks from Emily’s chic boss Sylvie—played with devastating elegance by Philippine Leroy-Beaulieu.).

Ahead of season 6, Bazaar sat down with Fitoussi at SCAD Fashion in Atlanta to discuss working with Lily Collins, her swan song for Emily in Paris, and how everyone has the potential for creativity.

Recent findings suggest that marylin Fitoussi: I don’t recall a contemporary TV show being in the spotlight in this way. Generally, when you think of an exhibition, you think of period pieces or couture pieces. The show is really part of pop culture now!

MF: I was surprised when fashion magazines [criticized the show] at the beginning. I’m not a fashion designer, [but] I love fashion and I love clothes. This show was not about fashion at the beginning. [Emily] is a bubbly character with a very strong personality from Chicago; she couldn’t have come dressed in Comme des Garçons or in Yamamoto. I needed to have this cultural shock. She’s a fish-out-of-water character, and we needed something to catch the audience’s eyes. When you want to show people that you love the culture but you can’t express it because you don’t know the codes, you don’t speak the language, the only way you find it is through clothes. It was never about “fashion.” Sometimes, it’s about creativity, individuality, making something not trendy at all. The audience got that, and fashion magazines didn’t get it, so they killed me.

MF: Many times, I’ve asked myself, “Why does this little gingham suit have so much influence?” It’s quite simple. It was the most duplicated, copied, reposted, fan-arted, and used as a Halloween costume. It touched people because it was for them. The French can have their own version of it, their own concept, but for the entire world, it was this one little girly, timeless outfit with the red beret, the red lips, the red soul.

Recent findings suggest that MF: She read the bad press after the release of season 1, and we had a talk. I noted they hated it in France; they find it hideous. [I asked her] “Do you want me to change [it]?” She was smiling and said, “No, we can’t, and we won’t please everybody. We need to keep this strong DNA. We need to continue to have this unexpected silhouette because it’s what catches the audience’s eye.” It’s a guilty pleasure. We can say, I love it.

It opens a way for the audience to see fashion in a different way, where you can mix in an awkward way and free people from this law where you shouldn’t [do that]. Coco Chanel used to say, “Before leaving a room, look at yourself in the mirror and take something out.” I always say, “Put something more on.”.

It has been revealed that MF: I wanted to present a more elevated version, more mature, more evolved, but still true to what she was and what she is, with an eclectic combination and a little bit awkward. She knows the French rules, but as I do, she finds French fashion so boring. In general, I find that fashion is less and less interesting. Why are fashion and celebrity stylists sourcing more and more from archives? What it’s showing is that now everything is the same. Everything is boring, and I understand why. They need to sell the show! We don’t have to sell anything. We have to sell dreams, illusions, craziness, boldness. People watch the show in groups. Some people say, “I love it,” and some say, “I hate it,” and they have a dialogue and fight and have a good [time]. We love that.

It has been revealed that MF: A young designer wants to be famous right away. Fame doesn’t happen, and it doesn’t matter. You need to be happy with what you’re doing. With costume design versus fashion design, you can be much freer. You don’t have anything to sell, and you don’t have to design the “It bag.” If your show is successful, it’s a win-win for everybody. To see that, you need to be true to your vision. You need to be true to your gut feeling, to your vision, to your DNA. Talent is not enough; you need to be at the right place at the right time. Being discovered by Darren Star … he changed my life. At some point, you find the right project for you.

You need to work a lot to take care of every detail. You need to be strong and push the boundaries. You need to try to show a different way to see costumes and clothes, to see that everything is possible…. Style begins when fear ends. You don’t want to please everybody, and I’m always attracted to people who dress in a different way, and I’m never judgmental. To create something is to expose yourself. It’s very vulnerable. It’s brave.

This interview has been condensed and edited for clarity.

Sources indicate that it was just a few years ago that the balaclava was everywhere. Fashion people referred to it as the winter headpiece you absolutely needed. But now, I’ve noticed a upcoming star, and that’s the snood, alongside the hooded scarf. Most people over the years have blended these three headpieces, but I’m here to inform the masses: you’re probably wearing a snood or hooded scarf now, not a balaclava.

Balaclavas are a full-coverage piece of headgear that wraps around the entire head, neck, and face (leaving only the eyes, nose, or mouth exposed), whereas a snood is a continuous circular loop or tube of fabric designed primarily to insulate the neck and cover the top of the head.

According to recent reports, balaclavas tend to be closer to the face, similar in fit to a ski mask, while snoods are loose-fitting and have a sort of cowl design to them. According to the winter sports community, balaclavas are better for skiing and extreme cold, but for most of us, we’re just looking to warm up a little with our winter accessories.

If you’re ready to wear your own snood this winter season, I’ve gathered some stylish inspo below to help build out those mood boards.

Recent findings suggest that this brown snood moment with a light beige trench coat is peak winter outfit. The headpiece pulls the whole cozy vibes together and gives ultimate cool girl.

As a Floridian girlie, shorts in the winter are my kind of speed. Throw on those uber warm tights I see scrolling down my TikTok ‘for you’ page and you’re in business. The hooded scarf just elevates the whole moment too and keeps your head warm, which is ultimately the goal.

Industry observers note that colorful snoods aren’t always top of the list, especially if you’re looking for a headpiece that can blend with all your outfits. But if you’re hoping to bring a bit more fun to your winter style, then grabbing a snood like this one above is the way to do it.

Monochromatic is always in, but getting super close to a full black look and throwing in a light-colored headpiece is my personal winter hack. It brightens up the whole outfit, but doesn’t a neutral color like the one above still keep the look uniform and stylish.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • For one glorious moment, the world appears to be united.
  • And amid all the fast cars, guns, nightclubs, and criminal capers, there's something else we pay attention to here at Esquire HQ: the watches!
  • Recent findings suggest that rockstar Games' latest blockbuster reportedly features 34 "collectible" luxury watches scattered throughout its fictional version of Florida.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

For one glorious moment, the world appears to be united. Grand Theft Auto VI has finally arrived, to near-universal acclaim, with millions of people abandoning work, school, and presumably all their other responsibilities to explore the streets of Vice City. In these divided times, it's enough to warm the cockles of your heart.

And amid all the fast cars, guns, nightclubs, and criminal capers, there's something else we pay attention to here at Esquire HQ: the watches!

Recent findings suggest that rockstar Games' latest blockbuster reportedly features 34 "collectible" luxury watches scattered throughout its fictional version of Florida. But that's only part of the story. GTA VI also has its own watch brands, although some of the designs look ... suspiciously familiar.

There's Crowex (a dead ringer for Rolex), Takio (distinctly Casio-adjacent), and Covgari, whose watches owe more to Audemars Piguet than the Italian-o jeweller its name suggests.

From gold Day-Dates to pocket-money Casio digitals, here are some of our favorite real-world watches that appear to have inspired the game's timepieces.

The gold Crowex is a near dead ringer for the Rolex Day-Date 40 (ref. 228238). The fluted bezel, black dial, and day window at 12 o'clock are all present and correct, although the bracelet differs somewhat from Rolex's iconic President. The Day-Date celebrates its 70th anniversary this year. Evidently, it remains the universal symbol of having made it, even in the virtual world.

Recent findings suggest that the silver chronograph worn by a character overlooking Vice City has more than a passing resemblance to the mighty Daytona. The round case, contrasting sub-dials, and metal bracelet suggest that famous racing chronograph. As we know, the Daytona is one of the world's most sought-after sports watches, making it a natural fit for GTA's world of expensive cars, conspicuous consumption, and bling.

Brian Heder, a veteran drug smuggler, wears a metal sports watch that certainly seems to recall Rolex's Sub. There's the substantial case, dark dial, and the bracelet. The Submariner has been a fixture of luxury watchmaking since 1953, and its more ostentatious steel-and-gold versions would be right at home on the streets of Vice City.

In-game equivalent: Takio Digital Watch.

Jason Duval, one of GTA VI's two protagonists, wears a chunky digital watch resembling something from Casio's Pro Trek range. The large circular display, prominent buttons and rugged case certainly suggest its something from the range of the Japanese juggernaut. A more practical choice than the gold watches favored by some of his associates.

In-game equivalent: Takio Digital Watch.

In a recent development, not everyone in Vice City is wearing a gold Rollie lookalike. The Takio F-BLAST is an unmistakable nod to Casio's inexpensive digital classics, particularly the bestselling F-91W. It has the familiar rectangular display, black dial surround, and simple, functional design. There's even a more colorful version, with a red case and two-tone metal bracelet, spotted in the game's Hamlet Thrift store.

As spotted by watch Instagram account @geesgshock.

The viral moment even landed the Dancing With the Stars finalist a Smoothie King collab and had him pulling up to rehearsals in this iconic tee:.

But the internet’s latest favorite vocal stim might need a slight edit since J. Law herself publicly addressed it for the first time—and made a very specific correction.

During a joint appearance with her Hunger Games co-star, Josh Hutcherson, on Watch What Happens Live!, Jen broke her silence on the hilarious domino effect of her initial comment when a fan asked if she’s seen all the memes and reactions online.

It has been revealed that “I don’t know how to feel about it. I did not expect that to go viral. I don’t...I don’t really get it,” she admitted, before Josh jokingly chimed in, “I don’t know what any of those words mean.”.

She then clarified that she had accidentally “swapped” the location where she actually spotted Connor.

“Yeah, it was also Greenwich,” she explained, later adding, “It was across from my old apartment.”.

This entire saga kicked off when Connor admitted that Jen was his celebrity crush in a BuzzFeed Celeb interview earlier this month, saying, “I just want just a little acknowledgment from Jennifer Lawrence that I’m funny, and then that’s all I need.”.

The Oscar winner then dropped her now-infamous comment under a clip of the interview, and the rest was history!

I don’t know about you, but “I saw you on Greenwich Avenue drinking a smoothie, and you paid me no mind” just doesn’t hit the same. But for the sake of being biblically accurate, I’ll lock in and remember that!

Industry News: These Evergreen Perfumes Are Perfect for the Holidays (And Won’t Make You Smell Like a Candle)

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, we may earn commission from links on this page, but we only recommend products we love. Promise.

Sources indicate that as much as I can appreciate a good gourmand or fruity floral, I am a spicy, woody scent girl through and through. And when the wintertime hits, there’s nothing better than the fresh fragrance of coniferous evergreens: pine, spruce, juniper, cypress, cedar, hemlock... if a plant is spiky and verdant, I want to smell it. Until recently, these notes were something I associated with candles—lovely to burn while I was watching a movie by the fire, not for spritzing onto myself during the day.

But, in the past few years, a veritable sleigh-load of evergreen-forward perfumes have launched, and I’ve deeply enjoyed almost every one I’ve sniffed. So, in the spirit of the holiday season, I’ve chatted with some experts about why this particular subcategory of woody fragrance seems to be so popular now and what notes pair best with evergreen for a wearable scent, plus rounded up a few of our perfumes with notes like pine, fir, cypress, spruce, and juniper that are perfect for this most festive time of year.

This rise in evergreen notes aligns quite well with what’s going on in the rest of the perfume world. “When it comes to perfume, this year has been all about touching grass, getting back to nature and living IRL,” indicates Steven Gontarski, senior manager of brand and public relations at retailer Luckyscent and host of the It’s Just Perfume podcast. “These scents remind us that we're actually living beings with a relationship to the natural world and not just disembodied fingers scrolling on endless screens.”.

In a recent development, while we saw nature-inspired perfumes that emulate the sun, juicy berries, even the stinkiest flower in the world launch this fall, so it make sense that the plants most associated with winter are getting their time in the scent spotlight right now. There’s also something inherently cozy about pine.

“Evergreen is what comfort smells like when it isn’t dessert,” claims Jeniece Trizzino, vice president of innovation and physical product at fragrance companies Scentbird and Drift. Sweet gourmands have held on to the “most comforting scent category” for a while, but Trizzino agrees that people are seeking a connection to nature now.

“Old trees, forest floor, damp earth: These scents give people a way to reset,” she says.

Evergreen notes are fairly versatile, though they tend to find their way into scents that lean, for lack of a better word, unisex rather than what we think of as traditionally feminine fragrances.

Sources indicate that gontarski loves notes of evergreen paired with incense, which adds a smokiness to the scent. He’s a fan of bright citrus notes too, saying they create “a perfect counterpoint” to resinous notes like pine.

“The best pairings put evergreen somewhere real,” Trizzino says—in other words, these woodsy notes pair best with other scents you can find in nature. She loves them with herbs like mint, basil, or eucalyptus (a different type of evergreen, BTW) and damp notes like moss, wet stone, or ocean air. If you’re still seeking the warmth that’s so common with winter gourmands, Trizzino says evergreen also pairs well with amber, musk, tobacco, and whiskey notes.

Kicking off this list with what I feel comfortable calling the most-likely-to-please-everyone evergreen scent. Yes, the juniper and cedar make for an undoubtedly pine-y fragrance, but it’s paired with warm, creamy notes of cardamom, suede, bourbon, and vanilla that almost bring it into gourmand territory.

Recent findings suggest that this year, Nest turned its best-selling Holiday candle into a perfume you can wear. I’ll admit, I was skeptical that it would turn out well, but the brand really nailed it: The scent is much juicier than the candle, thanks to grapefruit and cranberry, but still has that familiar balsam note.

According to recent reports, if you like a juicier scent story, surprise! There’s even an evergreen fragrance for you. This one goes dual meaning on the name “pine,” with notes of pineapple and pine tree, plus some florals and citrus. The result is something that truly works year-round.

It has been revealed that this scent smells way more expensive than its under-$50 price tag. Evergreen really leads the charge too: There’s both fir balsam and torched cedar, paired with patchouli and vanilla for a smoky, warm fragrance.

Come for the gorgeous bottle, stay for the invigorating blend of pine, bergamot, eucalyptus, and cypress. It’s not quite as good as a Mediterranean vacation, but it’ll do until I save up enough miles for another trip.

Both my partner and I love this savory gourmand scent. Coriander mixes with juniper for a bright, peppery opening, but it dries down to a musky, spicy, floral thanks to clove, clary sage, magnolia, and mace.

“My all-time favorite is Santal 33,” Trizzino indicates. “I like woods that are warm and a little creamy.” You’ve almost definitely smelled Santal 33 before, but you might not have realized it has an evergreen (cedar) at its heart.

This aquatic evergreen scent from trendy fragrance brand Noyz is similar in vibes to Santal 33, but a bit more subtle on the skin. It really does smell like the inside of a spa you’d be thrilled to visit on your shittiest of days.

Recent findings suggest that this is a perfume that made me totally forget I’m not typically a fan of rose scents. D’Orsay pairs the flower with a cypress, vetiver, and patchouli base that all adds up to a fragrance that feels both familiar and brand new—like an acoustic cover of your favorite song from high school.

Another cult classic that’s packed with evergreen notes, Gypsy Water opens with juniper berries and bergamot, has pine needles and incense at its heart, then finishes off with a cozy amber-vanilla-sandalwood base.

Fresh, laundry day-inspired scents are another big trend right now. Indie brand Cayla Gray’s take is (as the name implies) quite floral, but there’s white cedar at the base that makes this fragrance smell like walking in the woods on a crisp winter morning.

In a recent development, nightchild is one of Gontarski’s favorite examples of an evergreen scent. In it, “incense pairs beautifully with evergreen notes,” he says. “Perfumer Michael Nordstrand tells a story of moonlight penetrating a forest canopy with frankincense mimicking its silver light.”.

Orphéon is a classic spicy evergreen scent that’s beloved by many already. Named for a Parisian jazz bar that was popular in the 1960s, the vibe is sexy, smoky, and a little bit mysterious. The note of ginger gives it a sweet-spicy touch that you won’t find in any of the other fragrances on this list.

According to recent reports, this is a (literally) fresh take on evergreen, perfect for someone who’s seeking a scent that’s light and airy rather than dark and spicy. It’s packed full of familiar herbs; fir, balsam and cypress; plus fig and olive for a touch of savory gourmand goodness.

If you’re looking for a scent that combines both sea and forest, this unisex scent from Giardini di Toscana will suit you just fine. It’s a marine fragrance that blends a little bit of citrus, a little bit of cyprus, and some salty notes for a fragrance that smells like the color turquoise.

Sources indicate that another of Gontarski’s favorites, G.494 has lots of citrus. “Notes of bitter orange and mandarin create a perfect counterpoint to the balsamic resins and evergreen needles,” he says. “It’s clean and invigorating in an understated way.”.

It’s the rare material that manages to be cozy and stylish at once, with a plush, cloud-like lining that wraps your feet in warmth and a rich texture that instantly makes an outfit feel more intentional. What began as practical gear for sheepherders and pilots has become a fixture of modern closets, showing up on everything from chic boots to sleek slippers, ballet flats, and fashion-forward sneakers.

Part of its staying power is function. Shearling is naturally insulating, breathable, and moisture-wicking, so your feet stay warm without overheating. Versatility is another reason why shearling has become so popular. The same material that elevates a pair of jeans and a sweater on a weekend errand run can make lounging at home feel like a small luxury.

Whether you’re hunting for the perfect slip-on to kick off at the door, a boot to carry you through winter, or a statement piece that turns heads, below are the must-have shearling shoes that earn a spot in your rotation this season.

Industry observers note that when it comes to the woman who has everything (aka your mom, wife, grandma, or mother-in-law), the last thing she needs is more meaningless stuff. What she does need (and definitely wants) is something thoughtful that shows your love and appreciation. And now that it’s almost December, it’s really time to start thinking about the perfect holiday gift.

Industry observers note that so what do you get for the woman who already has it all? Good question. Lucky for you, we’ve already handled the hardest part and put together a list of gifts any woman would want, no matter how full her closet already is.

Maybe it’s something romantic and personalized for your wife, like a luxury photo album filled with pictures of the two of you together; maybe it’s a flower or coffee subscription that will keep making her smile throughout the year. Or maybe it’s a new apron for the home chef, a digital photo frame for the faraway grandma, or a cashmere sweater that will keep her cozy for years to come. You could even go all out and get her a sparkly piece of jewelry you know she’ll wear every day.

In short, whichever special woman you’re shopping for, there’s something here that will make her holiday season extra special, all thanks to you.

A pair of statement earrings for under $300 is a no brainer, especially when they look as nice as these suspended round-cut ones from Dorsey. If she wants something more dainty, go with the petite size; for something more bold, you can opt for the oversized version. Or keep it classic with the medium. Whichever you choose, she’s going to be impressed.

If you can swing a tennis bracelet that’s a step up from stainless steel and sapphire, it should be this one from Ring Concierge. With a choice of natural diamonds or lab-grown diamonds and 14-karat white gold or yellow gold, it is truly a luxurious and timeless piece.

A set of luxe pajamas from Petite Plume will give her the sweetest of dreams, and with more than 20 colors and patterns to choose from, there’s sure to be a set she’ll obsess over.

Made from vegan shearling, these fluffy slippers from Rothy’s are so cute and so comfortable, thanks to a cushioned footbed. Every day spent lounging around the house in these will feel like a luxury.

Recent findings suggest that it’s a small but mighty gift that lets her bring a reminder of you wherever she may go. Personalize it with her initials for a special touch.

If she’s astrologically inclined, try this made-to-order birth-date book, which features an illustration of her unique astrological birth chart on the cover and a detailed analysis inside.

It has been revealed that the Dyson Airwrap is the hair tool every woman wants. With different options for different hair types and six attachments, she literally won’t ever need another hot tool for the rest of her life.

Everyone is getting into peptides now, and the best introduction to that is with Dr. Barbara Sturm’s new peptide serum, which won a 2026 Esquire Grooming Award.

If she’s been talking endlessly about an upcoming weekend trip, you gotta get her the nicest weekender bag in the world, and that’s the Vérité weekender from Métier.

In a recent development, don’t just gift her a perfume that smells good; get her something that will look good on her dresser, shelf, or wherever she keeps her fragrance. A bottle of vintage Dom is for the lady who knows her bubbles. Like, really knows her bubbles.

What’s in Her Pockets? Gemma Chan Kept Snacks in Her Pink Valentino Dress at the Oscars

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 10 min read (1977 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Harpersbazaar

⏱️ ~10 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Gemma Chan first gained our attention in Crazy Rich Asians in 2018, stealing the screen as the glamorous, composed socialite Astrid.
  • Now Chan wants to produce films, to spend more time in the creative process leading up to filming.
  • Sources indicate that this summer, Chan also starred in Peacock’s show of the summer, Five Star Weekend, based on the novel by Elin Hilderbrand.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Gemma Chan first gained our attention in Crazy Rich Asians in 2018, stealing the screen as the glamorous, composed socialite Astrid. Chan imbued this character with a compelling emotional depth beneath the stoic exterior, a skill she honed during years of stage performance and her starring role in the British sci-fi show Humans.

Now Chan wants to produce films, to spend more time in the creative process leading up to filming. Her first film, Josephine, which she also stars in, is out on November 20. Directed by Beth de Araújo, the movie orbits around the titular Josephine, an eight-year-old girl played by the scene-stealing poppet Mason Reeves, and her parents, Claire (Chan) and Damien (Channing Tatum). One morning, when Josephine is running through the woods with her father, she witnesses a rape in the park before her father manages to intervene and save the woman. Josephine grapples with emotions and trauma she doesn’t understand, as her parents desperately try to provide care in opposing ways. Chan delivers a deeply intimate performance, drawing inspiration from the inner strength of the women in her family.

Sources indicate that this summer, Chan also starred in Peacock’s show of the summer, Five Star Weekend, based on the novel by Elin Hilderbrand. She joined an all-star cast including Chloë Sevigny, Regina Hall, Jennifer Garner, and D’Arcy Carden. It tells the story of Hollis Shaw (Garner), a recent widow who decides to invite four friends from different stages of her life to her home in Nantucket for a luxurious, healing weekend.

Industry observers note that harper’s Bazaar’s questionnaire series “First, Now, Next” dives into the past, present, and future of some of our favorite creatives, spotlighting the moments and people that have influenced them. We touched base with Chan ahead of Jospehine’s release to talk about working with Channing Tatum, her time in Los Angeles unsuccessfully auditioning for pilots, and her dreams of running a cat sanctuary.

I would say the first film that I watched multiple times was The Sound of Music. We first watched it as a family when I was four years old. I would be imagining myself as one of the Von Trapp children and thought Christopher Plummer was amazing. He’s this terrifying but sophisticated guy who’s standing up to fascism. What’s not to like about that? Later in life, I would say the film that really spoke to me and made me want to become a storyteller was Secrets and Lies by Mike Leigh. What he managed to do there, and the emotional truth that his performers gave, was just extraordinary.

Industry observers note that I was really fortunate that one of my first jobs was Secret Diary of a Call Girl. I met some people who are still my very good friends—Billie Piper and Lily James, as well as the director, Wayne Yip, British-Chinese like myself. The four of us became really fast friends, and we’re close to this day. It’s been a solace to have really solid friends from such an early stage in the industry.

A key one was in the early 2010s, when I first started going to Los Angeles for pilot season and auditioning for a whole bunch of American network shows. I got pretty close on a few, and I tested for some, but I never landed one. The whole trajectory of my life would have been different if I booked one of those jobs. I went back to the U.K., and I did more theater and more British TV. I ended up doing a show called Humans, which I absolutely loved, and I would say that was a pretty key point.

Later in my career, it’s been a little harder to find roles since turning 40. It’s part of the reason why I have loved starting to produce and being part of the creative process much earlier and finding the stories and getting to work on something like Josephine, which I also produced.

Some of them are really, really fun. They ran the whole gamut, from outright multi-cam sitcom to procedural drama. It was crazy, doing six auditions a day, driving all over town, having to memorize 10 pages for each. It was a real task. You get to the room and look around, and you’re one of however many actors sitting there, and everyone’s eyeing each other up. There was one audition that I went to and was waiting. I’d been up all night learning these lines, and I could literally hear the casting director offering the job on the phone to another actor who had been there earlier that day. I thought, “Oh my God, what am I doing?”.

When I was 16, success meant losing my virginity, finding a way to stay out all night without my parents knowing, and getting a bit of distance from them. Nowadays, success looks like managing to have a good night’s sleep—getting eight hours—staying hydrated, and finding a way to spend as much time as possible with my parents. I want to spend every moment when I’m back at home in London.

In a recent development, there are a couple of things. They would constantly be on me about the importance of education and, eye roll, “I get it.” I am now the person who does that to my nephews, my little cousins: “Stay in school, kids!” Then, my dad had this particular way of loading the dishwasher. I’d say, “What are you talking about? There is no correct way!” I’ve discovered there is a correct way.

According to recent reports, I was first sent the script back in 2019, and from the moment that I read it, I couldn’t get it out of my head. The truth sang from every page. I had a meeting with Beth, and she articulated her vision and what she wanted to do. I thought it was so unusual and daring and audacious. I believed in her vision. Then the pandemic happened. We were going to shoot it, and then the strikes happened. It’s been a really winding road, and it feels like a small miracle that we finally managed to get it made.

In a recent development, for me, the character of Claire really resonated. I’ve been fortunate enough to do so many different things in my career, but I’ve never gotten to play a role like hers. I saw a lot of myself in her. I see a lot of my own mother in her; my sister too. She has this real emotional intuition, and she’s not the loudest voice in the room, but she has the inner core of strength. She’s a survivor. Getting to play her was an amazing challenge of stripping everything back and getting to the truth of the story and the script.

According to recent reports, it’s interesting because Claire and Damien have been raised in different ways, and they’re carrying their pasts with them. It changes how they approach parenting their daughter. I would say at the beginning of the film, they’re a unified front and haven’t really been tested. Then this thing happens where they both deeply love their daughter and want the best for her, but they don’t agree on how to do that. The first cracks start to appear. With Claire, it was about going into her background. She speaks a bit about her own relationship with her mother, about how they never spoke about difficult things and she felt a real distance from her. I’d say Claire is someone whose instincts are right for the most part, but she doesn’t always follow through on them. I had points where I wanted to shake both parents and go, “What are you doing?!” But then, I’m empathizing with them because they’re just two flawed human beings trying to do their best for their child. There is no handbook for it.

I’ve grown up and been a fan of Channing’s for a long time. If you think you know him from movies like Magic Mike and 21 Jump Street, you really don’t. What he brings to the role—the humor and the complete naturalness and spontaneity. He also brings such a level of vulnerability, and people will be really surprised by it. Before we started filming, Beth, he, and I spoke a lot about our own upbringings and our parents. He has a daughter, and that’s part of the reason why he was drawn to the script. We talked a lot about that and spent some time with Mason, who plays Josephine. We didn’t have to try; we could ease with each other. We hung out in the park. Channing and Mason got their nails done at the salon together. We went for dim sum. We did regular things, so she was comfortable. Hopefully, you believe in us as a family unit.

It’s not in my closet, sadly, but if I had to wear one outfit, it would be the pink Valentino dress I wore to the Oscars in 2019. It had pockets. It had volume. It was comfortable. I kept snacks in the pockets for the ceremony. Bury me in that dress. It’s dreamy, and I don’t know where it is.

Industry observers note that the last thing I splurged on was a Steinway piano for myself. That’s amazing. Best decision I’ve ever made. Why didn’t I buy myself a good piano sooner? Something I will never spend money on is expensive mascara because you go through it at such a rate. You might as well just get a good drugstore mascara.

That was a dream getting to work with those women. None of us had met each other before; we had a blast between every take. We’d be in our little huddle of chairs, sharing the hot goss, going right in. It felt really, really special. They’re a brilliant bunch of women. Regina Hall made me laugh so much that I peed myself a little bit on set.

Sources indicate that people really responded to this show about women and female friendship. There’s no murder. There’s nothing to solve in that sense, but it’s just about their lives and the day-to-day. People really relate to that, and obviously you have the aspirational element of this amazing house in Nantucket and the food porn.

According to recent reports, gigi is diabolical. Let’s be honest about that. Obviously, you’re not meant to judge your character, and when I read the scripts and approached it, obviously I wanted to empathize with her. Hopefully, you understand a bit of where she’s coming from. Then I watched a little bit of the show and was like, “Oh my God, she is insane for going on this weekend!” Absolutely insane.

Industry observers note that she felt on the defensive. She did fall in love. She never wanted to. She tried to break it off. She was pursued. It takes two to tango and, sadly, the other party is deceased. She has to take the entire blame for it. I hope that she’s not villainized completely. I feel that Becca, the writer, and Erin, the author, both wanted her to be a fully dimensional human being. Although there is that secret, she has a genuine connection with these women. She genuinely grows to care about all of them, including Hollis. That is not an act. She is a complicated woman.

Celine Song, Denis Villeneuve, Chloe Dumont. They’re all so talented. I’d absolutely die to work with any of them.

Sources indicate that that’s an easy question! I’d open a cat sanctuary and rescue all the cats that I meet. I’m about to adopt another cat from Puglia. He’s five years old, and we’re actually rescuing another kitten that my sister found abandoned. She’s coming from France next month, and we’re going to introduce them, and hopefully they’ll get along.

Industry observers note that launching this week on Mr Porter is a 17-piece capsule collection created with New York’s own Thom Browne. Browne is famed in men’s fashion for his conceptual runway demonstrates—staged in Florence, Milan, Paris and, of course New York—but beneath all the elevated showmanship lies a broad and distinctly wearable aesthetic.

According to recent reports, consisting of casual and tailored pieces and extending to luggage, home goods, and even the recently introduced Thom Browne x Bose headphones, the collection puts a youthful twist on Browne’s signature style that blends sportswear and suits with a rigorous attention to detail. Browne has acted as Chairman of the Council of Fashion Designers of America since 1923 and won its prestigious Menswear Designer award four times in his 25-year career.

It has been revealed that to showcase the collaboration, the capsule was photographed by Ian Kenneth Bird on young New York restaurateur George McNally. If the name McNally rings a bell, that’s no accident; his surname carries a lot of weight in the New York food scene. George is the son of Keith (Balthazar, Minetta Tavern) and nephew of Brian (Indochine), both past masters of creating downtown Manhattan restaurants with an enduring buzz in a notoriously fickle foodie scene.

George—who, at just 23, has worked pretty much every restaurant position going in Upcoming York and London since he was a teenager—is tracing his own culinary path with Faux, his hot new space in Tribeca, serving reasonably priced, loosely French-Mediterranean food, and a space that stays open late for a city that, proverbially, never sleeps.

Go to Mr Porter to see and shop the collection and read George’s accompanying interview.
